question: US-Iran 60 day negotiation period extended?
resolution_criteria:
On June 14, 2026, the United States and Iran announced a written diplomatic agreement (the MOU), including a 60-day negotiation period toward a “final deal”, extendable by mutual consent.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if both the United States and Iran publicly and officially announce an extension of the 60-day negotiation period initiated by the MOU between market creation and August 20, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of a present extension of the 60-day negotiation period, a previously-unannounced prior extension of the 60-day negotiation period, or definitive agreement to extend the 60-day negotiation period.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify an extension of the 60-day negotiation period initiated by the MOU. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an extension, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. However, the announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the MOU by name.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The extension must be mutually announced by the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Mutual announcement means that taken together, the announcements from the United States and the Islamic Republic of Iran directly indicate that both parties have agreed to extend the 60-day negotiation period, or have recognized a definitive extension of the period.

The following do not qualify as official announcements: 
- Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official; 
- Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States or Iran;
- Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States or Iran will announce or implement an extension of the 60-day negotiation period; 
- Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; 
- Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional extension of the 60-day negotiation period rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once an extension has been mutually announced by the United States and Iran, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the extension is ever actually implemented.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States and Iran, including their official representatives.
research:
I found no joint official US-Iran announcement extending the 60-day period as of 2026-08-07. Both sides have treated the memorandum as broken since mid-July. Several search results were published after 2026-08-07, and I left them all out as instructed. Many direct page fetches were blocked by the proxy, so most items below come from search-result summaries rather than full articles.

## 1. Resolution source
- No single URL or data series decides this. Resolution depends on official US and Iranian statements, such as the White House, Trump's posts, the State Department, Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei and FM Araghchi.
- 2026-06-17: CNN published the US release of the 14-point memorandum. It commits both sides to "negotiating and achieving the final deal in a maximum 60 days extended with mutual consent." [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/17/middleeast/us-iran-war-mou-text-intl), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamabad_Memorandum)
- Sources disagree on the start date, which changes when the 60 days run out:
  - The market says it was announced June 14.
  - Wikipedia says it was signed June 17.
  - Iran International says it was signed June 18 and took effect June 19.
  - That puts the end of the window around Aug 13 to Aug 18, before the Aug 20 market deadline. [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202607080326)

## 2. Current status
- Neither side had officially announced an extension by 2026-08-07, and I found no report of one.
- The memorandum has been publicly declared "over" by Trump and "suspended" by Iran (see section 3). That makes a formal mutual extension harder to arrange, but the period can still be extended by mutual consent.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-05: Trump said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could come "tomorrow or the next day." Iran said it was negotiating with Oman, not the US, and its Foreign Ministry spokesman said an Iran-Oman shipping text was in "final stages." A Gulf official put the chance of a deal by Friday at 50-50. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/05/us-iran-war-trump-hormuz-bessent-iran-deal-close.html), [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/trump-says-deal-to-reopen-the-strait-of-hormuz-could-come-as-early-as-wednesday), [CNN live](https://www.cnn.com/2026/08/05/world/live-news/iran-war-trump)
- 2026-08-05: Axios reported calls among Witkoff, Araghchi and Oman's foreign minister. It said Iranian leadership had approved a Hormuz arrangement and the US was aiming for a Wednesday announcement. I could not fetch the article to check whether it mentions the memorandum's 60-day period. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/05/us-iran-strait-of-hormuz-deal-nears), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/8/5/iran-oman-us-close-to-hormuz-deal-what-do-they-all-want)
- About 2026-08-01 to 08-03: Secondary sources say Trump paused planned strikes at mediators' request and said the "parameters" of a deal were being discussed. [Fox News live](https://www.foxnews.com/live-news/iran-war-news-trump-israel-august-3), [CryptoBriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/trump-reports-productive-iran-talks-amid-2026-conflict-negotiations/)
- 2026-07-31: Diario Las Americas reported that Trump was weighing sending the memorandum to Congress, describing it as extending the ceasefire by 60 days. I could not open the article to verify the details. [Diario Las Americas](https://www.diariolasamericas.com/eeuu/trump-sopesa-enviar-el-memorando-entendimiento-alcanzado-iran-al-congreso-su-revision-n5397311)
- 2026-07-20: Baghaei said Iran would keep its commitments only if the US kept its own, calling the memorandum otherwise "a piece of paper." [Iran International](https://www.iranintl.com/en/202607203616), [Tehran Times](https://www.tehrantimes.com/news/528294/Iran-halts-MoU-commitments-over-US-violations)
- 2026-07-18: Deputy FM Gharibabadi said Iran had suspended its commitments under the memorandum, after US strikes that Iran said killed 50 people that month. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/18/iran-accuses-us-of-striking-critical-infrastructure-as-war-intensifies), [Middle East Eye](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/iran-declares-islamabad-agreement-suspended-blames-us-violations)
- 2026-07-08: In Ankara, after IRGC strikes on US targets in Bahrain and Kuwait, Trump said: "As far as I'm concerned, it's over." He added that talks could continue. [WDTV](https://www.wdtv.com/video/2026/07/08/trump-us-iran-memorandum-its-over/)
- 2026-06-17/18: Trump said the 60 days was "not a hard deadline" and could run longer if Iran behaved. He also said the memorandum was "not final." [WRNO/iHeart](https://wrno.iheart.com/content/2026-06-18-trump-indicates-iran-deal-timeline-flexible/), [KXAN/The Hill](https://www.kxan.com/hill-politics/trump-60-days-not-a-hard-deadline-on-iran-negotiations/amp/)
- Iranian officials have also said publicly that the memorandum sets no binding "60-day deadline." I could not confirm when the cited summary was published. [CryptoBriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/iran-islamabad-mou-with-us-lacks-60-day-deadline-amid-ongoing-talks/)

## 4. Base rates
- I found no formal base rate for official, mutually announced extensions of US-Iran deadlines.
- In this war, deadlines have usually been loosened informally rather than extended by joint official announcement:
  - The two-week ceasefire in April 2026 led to further truces. [Al Jazeera](https://aljazeera.com/news/2026/4/7/trump-suspends-iran-bombing-for-two-weeks-following-dire-threats)
  - The 60-day ceasefire extension in May was first reported as "tentative" and needed Trump's approval. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/5/28/us-and-iran-reach-tentative-deal-for-60-day-truce-extension-officials-say)
- In the 2025 episode, Trump said Iran had "missed" a 60-day window. That deadline was let lapse rather than extended.
- Iran has consistently refused to call indirect contacts "negotiations." That pattern works against a clear Iranian official statement of the kind the criteria require.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has this exact market, "US-Iran 60 day negotiation period extended?", expiring Aug 20. [Orrery mirror](https://orrery.me/markets/us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-extended-20260624044855448), [Lines.com](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/politics/us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-extended-20260624044855448), [CoinGape](https://coingape.com/prediction-markets/will-us-iran-60-day-negotiation-period-be-extended/)
- A newsletter says the price traded between about 40% and 73% until 2026-08-06, then fell to the mid-20s. I could not confirm when it was published. [Pythia](https://pythia.beehiiv.com/p/new-post-5e95)
- An earlier report put the market at about 62%.
- I could not get a live price as of 2026-08-07, and I found no Kalshi or Manifold equivalent or expert forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Around Aug 13 to 18: the 60-day period ends, depending on whether it is counted from June 14, 17 or 19. Any extension, or a statement on the deadline from either side, would most likely come around then.
- The pending Hormuz deal (Iran, Oman, US) could either restart the memorandum track or replace it. A deal announced only through Oman would not count as a mutual US-Iran extension announcement.
- Watch for:
  - Baghaei's weekly press briefings, usually on Mondays.
  - Trump's statements and posts.
  - Pakistani, Omani and Qatari mediator statements. These do not count on their own; the criteria require official announcements from both governments.
- Risk of renewed US strikes or IRGC retaliation. The August pause was conditional.

That pushes me slightly below the market.
